pending_commit.commit_message: [autotest] Make stable_version handle empty image type If the stable_version command were asked to list mappings for an image type where there were no mappings to print, the command would fail with an exception. This could happen in some out of the way cases, such as with the staging instance. This fixes the handling to print nothing when there is nothing to print. CHROMIUM: iwl7000: Fail fast if HW is inaccessible at probe If the HW is not responding at probe time, fail immediately complaining about it. Without this, we see that the kernel spends > 100ms trying to load firmware (even gives an incorrect impression that it actually loaded a firmware) and do unnecesary processing before concluding that the device is not accessible: INFO kernel: [ 34.092678] iwlwifi 0000:01:00.0: enabling device (0000 -> 0002) WARNING kernel: [ 34.093560] iwlwifi 0000:01:00.0: Direct firmware load for iwl-dbg-cfg.ini failed with error -2 INFO kernel: [ 34.111523] iwlwifi 0000:01:00.0: loaded firmware version 17.318154.0 op_mode iwlmvm INFO kernel: [ 34.173250] iwlwifi 0000:01:00.0: Detected Intel(R) Dual Band Wireless AC 7265, REV=0xFFFFFFFF ERR kernel: [ 34.198023] iwlwifi 0000:01:00.0: iwlwifi transaction failed, dumping registers ERR kernel: [ 34.198044] iwlwifi 0000:01:00.0: iwlwifi device config registers: Signed-off-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@google.com> BUG=b:78586198 TEST=check it fails sooner if HW not accessible. Change-Id: I4fb5fea510961f18ee1bc1404ee7f85a7c40b22e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1031772 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luca Coelho <luciano.coelho@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org>

pppd: Patches to allow starting as non-root user. This CL is in preparation to run the shill process tree as a non-root user. It doesn't change any current functionality, but will let us run ppp as user "shill" in the future. In order to run pppd as a non-root user, we need to do two things: 1) Omit checks in startup code that asserts that pppd is running with root privs. 2) Allow to configure pppd at compile time to use a different runtime data directory than the default, which is /var/run, since pppd will soon run in a minijail under 'shill' user and we do not want to give 'shill' user access to /var/run. Patch #2 isn't in appropriate shape to upstream, so more work would need to be done there if we want to do that. That being said, the last version of ppp to be released was in 2014. BUG=chromium:649417 TEST=tested as part of larger sandbox shill debug CL Change-Id: Ifa9f2f785e74b9de8f3b9f4bc4f68c53d8b8e0ed Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1022398 Commit-Ready: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Tested-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org>
